content_of_post_to_comment:
Before you even stretch, say a prayer, drink a glass of water, or take a moment to appreciate a new day, your hand is already reaching for your phone! 😂🙋🏽‍♀️
You check WhatsApp, scroll through Facebook, watch TikTok videos, respond to messages, check emails, and before you know it, 30 minutes have disappeared! 😩
But have you ever stopped to think about how addicted we’ve become to our devices?
Our phones have become the first thing we reach for in the morning and the last thing we put down at night. We wake up and immediately invite notifications, other people’s opinions, news, and endless content into our minds before we’ve even had a moment with ourselves.
**The scary part? We sometimes spend more time looking at our screens than actually living our lives.**
Technology is a blessing, no doubt. It helps us connect, learn, work, and grow. But when we can’t sit in silence without checking our phones, enjoy a meal without taking pictures, or have a conversation without looking at a screen, it’s worth asking ourselves: *Are we using our devices, or are our devices using us?* 🤔
Here’s a little challenge for you: Tomorrow morning, give yourself the first 30 minutes of your day before giving your attention to your phone. Pray, meditate, stretch, journal, enjoy your coffee, or simply sit in peace.
You might be surprised by how much calmer and more present you feel. ❤️
**Your phone deserves your attention, but it doesn’t deserve the first and last moments of your every day.**
Now, let’s be honest in the comments! 😂👇🏽
comment: I noticed the part about not being able to sit in silence without checking your phone. I think that’s where a lot of us underestimate the habit, because it’s not just screen time but our discomfort with having an empty moment. I’ve found leaving my phone in another room for the first part of the morning makes the choice easier instead of relying on willpower.
